name: Lalmonirhat
tagline: Teesta's barrage, the corridor that crosses a border, and Kakina — the lost cultural capital of north Bengal.

guide.bestTime: October to March (cool, dry; the Teesta calm and the chars accessible)
guide.gettingThere: By train to Lalmonirhat Junction on the far-northern line, or by road from Dhaka (~9–10 hr) and Rangpur (~1.5 hr). No airport — the nearest is Saidpur (Nilphamari), ~50 km south.
guide.difficulty: Easy — flat terrain, short upazila hops; Patgram is a long but rewarding drive north for Burimari and Tin Bigha.

mustVisit.name: Tin Bigha Corridor & Dahagram–Angarpota
mustVisit.description: A 178 × 85 metre sliver of Indian land that India keeps permanently open to give Bangladesh road access to its Dahagram–Angarpota enclaves — one of the most curious pieces of geography in South Asia.
mustVisit.history: The corridor goes back to the 1974 Indira–Mujib treaty; after long delay India leased the strip to Bangladesh in 1992, and made it 24-hour open in 2011. Dahagram–Angarpota, the world's largest Bangladeshi exclave (about 22 sq km), sits inside India and is reached only through this lane.

practical.hours: Corridor lane open 24 hr (since 2011); BD-side checkpoint hours during daylight

howToReach.fromDistrictTown: About 55 km north of Lalmonirhat town in Patgram Upazila, near Dahagram union
howToReach.transport: Car or microbus from Lalmonirhat / Patgram

tips: Photography of border infrastructure is restricted — keep your camera down at the lane itself
Carry NID; the corridor crossing is logged on both sides
Dahagram is Bangladesh — you do not need an Indian visa to use the corridor lane

mustVisit.name: Teesta Barrage at Doani (Hatibandha)
mustVisit.description: The barrage that controls Bangladesh's share of the Teesta — the country's largest irrigation project, with a long row of gates spanning the river and a wide reservoir behind.
mustVisit.history: Commissioned to irrigate the northern Teesta floodplain, the barrage is the engineering centrepiece of the district and a fixed point in the politics of the Teesta water-sharing question. The downstream embankments are popular evening walks.

howToReach.fromDistrictTown: At Doani, Hatibandha Upazila, ~40 km north-west of Lalmonirhat town
howToReach.transport: Bus or microbus to Hatibandha, then easybike to Doani

tips: Best light is the hour before sunset
Heavy security — do not climb onto the operational structures

mustVisit.name: Burimari Land Port (Patgram)
mustVisit.description: Bangladesh's northernmost major land port — the official crossing into Changrabandha in West Bengal, and a key corridor for trade with Bhutan and Nepal via the Siliguri belt.
mustVisit.history: An old colonial railway station town that grew into a full customs port. Today freight and cross-border traffic move through here daily, and the zero-point gate is a working spectacle.

practical.hours: Immigration ~6 am – 6 pm; viewing area in daylight
practical.entryFee: Free; crossing needs valid passport and Indian visa

howToReach.fromDistrictTown: About 65 km north of Lalmonirhat town in Patgram Upazila
howToReach.transport: Direct bus from Lalmonirhat / Rangpur to Burimari

tips: Photography of fence infrastructure is restricted
Carry NID or passport even if you are not crossing
Pair with Tin Bigha Corridor on the same northern run

mustVisit.name: Kakina Zamindar Bari (Kaliganj)
mustVisit.description: The two-storey brick palace of the Roy Chowdhuris of Kakina — a fusion of European façades and Mughal ornament, with a royal court, guest wing, hawakhana and hidden passages.
mustVisit.history: Founded in the late 17th century by Raja Ram Narayan, the estate was expanded under Mahimaranjan Roy Chowdhury into the cultural and economic heart of northern Bengal. Mahimaranjan was the founding president of the Rangpur Literary Society, donated land for a theatre, and saw the railway stations of Mahimaganj, Teesta, Mahendranagar, Lalmonirhat, Aditmari, Mogolhat and Kakina all open under the Kakina Zamindari. The estate was auctioned off around 1925 after years of financial decline.

howToReach.fromDistrictTown: About 15 km south-west of Lalmonirhat town in Kaliganj Upazila

tips: Pair with poet Sheikh Fazlul Karim's house in the same village
Interior is unsafe — view from outside; the hawakhana is the best-preserved wing

mustVisit.name: Tushbhandar Zamindar Bari (Kaliganj)
mustVisit.description: A second old zamindar's mansion in Kaliganj — quieter than Kakina, with carved doorways, a family temple and broad tanks set among palm groves.

howToReach.fromDistrictTown: About 18 km south-west of Lalmonirhat town in Kaliganj Upazila

tips: Easy to fold into the same morning as Kakina
The local easybike drivers know the back lane in

mustVisit.name: Lalmonirhat WWII Airfield
mustVisit.description: A long-abandoned World War II British airbase on the southern edge of Lalmonirhat town — a relic of the Burma campaign, with a wartime runway still legible across the field, and now home to a Bangladesh Air Force unit and aviation training academy.
mustVisit.history: Built by the British during the Second World War to support operations against the Japanese in Burma, it sat unused for decades after independence. In recent years it has been revived as a Bangladesh Air Force base and the seat of Bangladesh's aerospace and aviation training programme.

practical.hours: Public viewing from the boundary road only; the base itself is restricted military property

howToReach.fromDistrictTown: On the southern edge of Lalmonirhat town

tips: Do not photograph the active base — only the public-road frontage
The history is in the scale of the runway, not in interpretive signs

specialties.name: Pelka
specialties.description: The earthy north-Bengal greens-and-kalai-flour curry — a Rangpur-belt home-cooking tradition that Lalmonirhat shares with Kurigram and Thakurgaon.

specialties.name: Kolai Ruti & Sidol Bhorta
specialties.description: Thick gram-flour rotis served hot with pungent fermented-fish sidol bhorta — the standard farmer's breakfast across the Teesta belt.

specialties.name: Kakina Literary Heritage
specialties.description: The Kakina Zamindari under Mahimaranjan Roy Chowdhury became a centre of Bengali letters in northern Bengal — patron of the Rangpur Literary Society and home of poet Sheikh Fazlul Karim, who set up his Shahabia Printing Works in Kakina in the 1900s.

specialties.name: Teesta Embankment Picnics
specialties.description: The cool months bring families and college groups to the embankments below the Teesta Barrage for picnics and slow afternoons over the reservoir.

bucketlist.title: Cross the Tin Bigha Corridor into Dahagram
bucketlist.detail: A 178 × 85 metre lane of India that's kept permanently open so Bangladeshis can reach Dahagram–Angarpota — the world's largest Bangladeshi exclave, all 22 square kilometres of it.

bucketlist.title: Walk the Teesta Barrage at Doani
bucketlist.detail: The largest irrigation project in Bangladesh — a long row of gates spanning the Teesta, with a wide reservoir behind it and embankments for evening walks.

bucketlist.title: See the gate at Burimari Land Port
bucketlist.detail: Bangladesh's northernmost major land port, the working road artery toward Changrabandha in West Bengal and onward toward Bhutan and Nepal.

bucketlist.title: Explore the Kakina Zamindar Bari
bucketlist.detail: The late-17th-century palace of the Kakina Roy Chowdhuris — European façade, Mughal detail, royal court, hawakhana and hidden passages. The cultural heart of north-Bengali letters in its day.

bucketlist.title: Visit poet Sheikh Fazlul Karim's home village
bucketlist.detail: Kakina was the home and life's work of Sheikh Fazlul Karim (1882–1936), who set up his Shahabia Printing Works here and wrote some 58 books before his death. His house and grave still stand.

bucketlist.title: See the Tushbhandar Zamindar Bari
bucketlist.detail: A quieter second zamindar's mansion in Kaliganj — carved doorways, broad tanks, and a family temple under palm groves.

bucketlist.title: Drive past the WWII Lalmonirhat Airfield
bucketlist.detail: A British wartime base built for the Burma campaign, abandoned for decades, now revived as the seat of Bangladesh's aerospace training. The old runway still runs across the field.

bucketlist.title: Eat fresh Teesta river fish
bucketlist.detail: Carp and catfish straight from the Teesta — the simplest northern plate, with mustard oil and a little green chili.

bucketlist.title: Try pelka at a home-style canteen
bucketlist.detail: The earthy north-Bengal greens-and-kalai-flour curry — slow-simmered, traditional, almost unheard of south of Rangpur division.

bucketlist.title: Eat kolai ruti with sidol bhorta
bucketlist.detail: Thick gram-flour rotis with pungent fermented-fish sidol bhorta — the breakfast that fuels the Teesta-belt bazaars.

bucketlist.title: Buy aakher gur at a winter haat
bucketlist.detail: Northern Bengal's sugarcane molasses, pressed and boiled at village mills — for tea and winter pithas.

bucketlist.title: Watch the trains roll through Lalmonirhat Junction
bucketlist.detail: Lalmonirhat Junction is the railway heart of north-western Bangladesh — the lines and yards remain a working monument to the British-era Kakina Zamindari that helped open them.

foods.name: Pelka
foods.description: Earthy regional curry of greens cooked with small kalai-flour balls — a north-Bengal home-cooking staple.

foods.name: Kolai Ruti
foods.description: Thick gram-flour rotis served hot with sidol bhorta or pickle — the farmer's breakfast across Rangpur division.

foods.name: Sidol Bhorta
foods.description: Pungent fermented-fish mash, pounded with red chili, onion and mustard oil — the partner to kolai ruti.

foods.name: Teesta River Fish
foods.description: Fresh catch from the Teesta — carp and catfish in light mustard curries.

foods.name: Aakher Gur
foods.description: Sugarcane molasses pressed and boiled at village mills — for winter pithas and tea.

foods.name: Aakher Gur Pitha
foods.description: Winter rice pithas — chitoi and bhapa — drizzled with fresh sugarcane molasses.

foods.name: Char Maize (Bhutta)
foods.description: Corn from the Teesta chars, grilled on the cob at the riverside ghats.

famousPeople.name: Sheikh Fazlul Karim
famousPeople.knownFor: Bengali poet and writer born at Kakina Bazar in Lalmonirhat in 1882. Wrote some 58 books across Bangla literature, founded the Shahabia Printing Works at Kakina, and was decorated with the titles 'Sahitya Bisharad', 'Kabya Ratnakar' and 'Neeti Bhushan'. A contemporary of Kazi Nazrul Islam, Begum Rokeya and Ismail Hossein Siraji.

didYouKnow: Lalmonirhat became a district on 1 February 1984, carved out of greater Rangpur; its five upazilas include Patgram in the far north, almost an island of Bangladesh between India and Bhutan.
The Tin Bigha Corridor is a 178 × 85 metre lane of Indian land kept open so Bangladesh can reach Dahagram–Angarpota, the world's largest Bangladeshi exclave (~22 sq km).
The Teesta Barrage at Doani is the largest irrigation project in Bangladesh, controlling the country's share of the Teesta.

The Kakina Zamindari under Mahimaranjan Roy Chowdhury was an early-20th-century cultural hub of northern Bengal — founding home of the Rangpur Literary Society, and patron of seven railway stations through Lalmonirhat.
Poet Sheikh Fazlul Karim (1882–1936) was born at Kakina Bazar in this district and set up his Shahabia Printing Works there.
Lalmonirhat's WWII-era British airfield is being revived as the seat of Bangladesh's aerospace and aviation training programme.
